assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED is the architecture that made superconducting circuits a controllable quantum-optics platform: strong coupling of a single artificial atom to a single microwave photon, dispersive readout and photon-mediated qubit coupling. Original, conceptually clear and the basis of most present superconducting processors and of the microwave quantum optics field. From my own subject area I regard its importance as very high, and it complements the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in circuits without duplicating it.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied the theoretical proposal with Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf; Wallraff, with Schoelkopf's group, delivered the first strong-coupling experiment; Schoelkopf's Yale group also drove transmon/readout development. Girvin and Devoret, who are central to the Yale effort and the prior prize, are not in the credited names, so the three-person configuration is defensible but leaves some credit questions. I should note my own proximity to this field when weighing it.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups over two decades and now industrial; the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely, with the 2025 prize on circuit macroscopic quantum phenomena not conflicting with it.
uncertainties: Exact credit split among Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf, Girvin and others such as Devoret is debatable.
My field proximity risks bias toward this candidate; I rely on the supplied candidate text and general knowledge, not independent verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by the HgTe observation of edge transport, opened topological band theory as a major branch of condensed matter physics. Originality, breadth and lasting impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theoretical core; Molenkamp's group carried out the decisive HgTe experiment following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Hasan's 3D ARPES work and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are also claimants, so a three-person prize leaves out serious contributors.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations and a mature, stable interpretation; recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Several worthy contributors (Hasan, Zhang, Bernevig, Hughes, Moore, Fu) cannot all be included.
I am not an expert in this area and rely on general knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstrations of ultra-low systematic uncertainty, reached fractional accuracy at the 1e-18 level. It is a clear, original and impactful invention supporting tests of fundamental physics and a possible redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength concept; Ye realised and refined strontium clocks to record performance. A two-person prize is a clean configuration, though Hall and Hänsch (comb) were already honoured in 2005 and other clock groups exist.
assessment.maturity: Very strong independent confirmation across many laboratories and stable interpretation; recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Overlap with other optical clock work (ion clocks, Hollberg and others) could blur attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of Hubbard-type models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and Fermi-Hubbard physics, gave a clean experimental route to many-body quantum matter. Important, widely adopted and conceptually clear.
assessment.attribution: The Jaksch et al. proposal by Zoller and Cirac and their colleagues is foundational but the experimentalists are the stronger prize trio from this list; Cirac and Zoller are better treated through B041 if at all. The five-name list cannot all be included, so the configuration is contested.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across many labs; a mature field. The Mott transition by Greiner and Bloch is solid; the connection to unresolved Hubbard-model questions is still developing.
uncertainties: Excluding the theorists Cirac and Zoller may be seen as unfair.
Whether the lasting impact is simulation of open questions or primarily technique remains open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-angle prediction and the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum materials. Originality and impact are very high and experimental follow-up is extensive.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald supplied the flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 observations. Cao and others in the experiment team, and Dean, Kim and Young, also made major contributions, so the allocation is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by multiple groups, but the origin of superconductivity and many correlated phases is still debated; this is somewhat early, though the core discovery is secure.
uncertainties: Allocation among theory, first experiment and later groups is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error-correcting codes and the topological code idea are the theoretical foundation for fault-tolerant quantum computing, which I regard as essential: full-scale error correction is the requirement for useful quantum processors. Clear and lasting intellectual impact.
assessment.attribution: Shor's 9-qubit code and Steane's codes plus Kitaev's toric code and fault tolerance are decisive; Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme and others are not credited, so attribution is incomplete for a physics prize.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations of below-threshold logical qubits are recent and encouraging, but practical fault tolerance is not yet established, so this is a bit early. Quantum information was recognised in 2022.
uncertainties: Whether the physics prize would see this as mathematical or computer science rather than physics.
Contested credit with Gottesman, Calderbank, Knill and Laflamme.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proposals for spin qubits in quantum dots and donors in silicon, and the experimental control of single electron spins, underpin a promising scalable platform compatible with semiconductor manufacturing. Significant, though less far-reaching than the leading superconducting or atomic platforms so far.
assessment.attribution: Loss and DiVincenzo proposed quantum-dot spin qubits; Kane proposed the donor nuclear-spin architecture; Vandersypen's group delivered key experimental advances. DiVincenzo is not in the credited names, so a gap remains. Other experimentalists (Kouwenhoven, Morello, Dzurak, Yacoby) are also important.
assessment.maturity: Experimental progress is strong with high-fidelity gates in silicon, but the platform has not yet demonstrated the scalability that would prove its decisive role. Recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: DiVincenzo missing from the credited names.
Platform competition leaves the long-term impact unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in iron pnictides opened a second family of unconventional high-Tc superconductors after the cuprates. Clear, surprising and broadly influential, though the pairing mechanism is not settled.
assessment.attribution: Kamihara and Hosono's 2008 report on LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx was the decisive discovery, with rapid follow-ups by Chinese groups, notably Ren and Chen, who are not credited here. A two-person prize is clean but leaves out those who raised Tc.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and mature after over a decade, though the theoretical interpretation remains debated and applications are limited.
uncertainties: Credit for rapid Tc increases by other groups is not covered.
